name: Opus 5 vol regime
strategy: Mid-vol re-risk after the equity-vol spike faded: residual long in integrated energy (XLE) plus a rate-factor spread of long large caps (SPY) against rate-and-margin-sensitive small caps (IWM), with 45% cash at 4% as a buffer while rate vol stays elevated.
reassessment_note: The 70% cash stance was explicitly conditional on VIX staying above 25, and that condition has lapsed. Per FRED/Cboe and Yahoo closes, VIX spiked to 28.18 on 11-05 (SPY -4.4%) and 25.64 on 11-06. It then fell to 19.92, 19.46, 17.49, 18.70 and 19.30 through 11-13, and the curve is back in contango (VIX9D 17.8 < VIX 19.3 < VIX3M 20.6). Equity vol is mid-regime, not crisis. The live stress has moved to rates: the 10y went from 4.86% on 11-09 to 5.15% on 11-13, and Trading Economics reports markets price a meaningful chance of a December Fed hike. That is the macro backdrop the small-cap short was built for. So I am re-risking partway rather than going fully invested. I raise gross from 30% to 55% and keep 45% cash because 10y rate vol and a still-elevated VIX (vs ~17 in October) argue against full exposure. I also pair the IWM short with a SPY long, so the book isolates the rate/size factor instead of carrying outright short beta into a contango, mean-reverting vol tape. Net dollar exposure is +5%, roughly beta-neutral given IWM's higher beta. Energy stays on: Brent rebounded from $91.49 (11-10) to $95.84 (11-13) and XLE recovered from $61.62 to $64.96. Research caveat: web search returned little dated news coverage for 11-09 to 11-13, so this rests mainly on index, yield and futures price data, plus the Cboe 11-09 weekly note and Trading Economics on hike odds.

positions.thesis: I raise the residual energy long from 12% to 15%. The oil leg washed out with Brent falling from about $117 (10-30) to $91.49 (11-10), and the flush looks done. Brent is back near $96 and XLE has rallied five straight sessions to $64.96. Geopolitical supply risk remains two-sided and that caps the size. The 8% stop sits below the 11-05/11-06 low of about $61.6, so the leg exits if the oil washout resumes.

I raise the small-cap short from 18% to 25% as the core rate-regime expression. The 10y jumped about 29bp in four sessions to 5.15% with December hike odds back in play, and that hits floating-rate, refinancing-heavy small-cap balance sheets hardest. IWM has already lagged since 11-11 ($283.09 to $277.54) while QQQ held near highs. The 8% stop caps the damage from a dovish Fed surprise squeezing small caps.

This is a new leg, the large-cap side of the rate/size spread. With VIX back below 20 and the curve in contango, keeping the small-cap short naked means paying for vol mean-reversion, which usually lifts the broad tape. Large caps with net cash balance sheets are less hurt by 5%+ yields than small caps, so SPY hedges the IWM short's beta and the book earns the spread. At 15% it is sized below the short to stay a little net short in beta-adjusted terms. The 7% stop (about $701) sits below the 11-05 panic close of $733 with room to spare and exits if a second equity-vol leg arrives.
